body:
What makes a real estate company good to work for?

Four things, in roughly this order: support (training, a manager who isn’t competing against you, real systems), economics (your take-home after every fee, not the headline split), culture (do people stay?), and brand (does the name help you win business?). A high split at a firm that gives you none of the first three is rarely the best place to work, only the best place to pay fees.

Why Adams, Cameron & Co. ranks for Daytona Beach Shores agents

Adams, Cameron & Co. has been the area’s largest brokerage since 1963, with around 300 agents and offices across Volusia and Flagler County, headquartered at 600 S. Atlantic Ave in Daytona Beach, minutes from Daytona Beach Shores. Daytona Beach Shores itself is a small, dense barrier-island town of about 5,200 people, made up largely of oceanfront condos, the kind of specialty coastal market where agents benefit even more from real support and a trusted name behind them. Agents cite the non-competing managers, the included marketing and technology, the training, and a genuine family culture. That’s why it appears on third-party “best places to work” lists. If support and a trusted local brand matter to you, it’s the established full-service choice.
